visualSystem.format: Vertical 9:16 with a food-first, mobile-native layout.
framing: Use tight close-ups where the finished bowl occupies most of the lower two-thirds.
Reserve the upper third for the primary claim so it remains separate from the food.
Mix food footage with one clean, full-frame information card rather than placing dense recipe text over moving food.
An occasional presenter or hand can enter from a side edge while the supporting chart or ingredient remains visible.
visualSystem.informationDensity: Alternate visually rich food shots with sparse headline overlays and a separate, denser evidence or ingredient card. Avoid combining a long ingredient list, method and nutrition table in one moving shot.
visualSystem.foodPlacement: Keep the bowl centered or slightly low, with the mozzarella, red passata and green spinach visible as distinct cues. Favor a close hero angle that makes one bowl feel abundant.
visualSystem.cameraStyle: Predominantly stable, close and direct: locked-off overhead or shallow high-angle preparation shots, followed by a low-to-mid high-angle hero close-up. Any movement should be restrained and motivated by stirring, spooning or revealing the cheese.
visualSystem.palette: Let tomato red, mozzarella white, bean cream and spinach green provide the color system against a quiet neutral surface. Use high-contrast white or dark text rather than decorative branding.

structure: Immediate finished-bowl hero and nutrition hook.
Fast ingredient identification using individual packs or measured ingredients.
Short preparation sequence focused on large, readable actions.
Return to the finished bowl for a spoon lift or texture reveal.
End on the complete one-bowl serving with the verification caveat.
shotRhythm.pacing: The references support a contrast between quick food-led shots and longer holds on dense informational frames. Keep action shots brief, but allow charts or ingredient cards enough time to scan.
shotRhythm.recommendedPattern: Hero → ingredients → assembly → information card → cheese/texture payoff → final claim.
shotRhythm.constraint: Exact cut duration cannot be determined from still reference frames.

firstSecond.visual: Open directly on the completed pizza-bean bowl, tightly framed, with visible melted mozzarella and passata. Use a spoon entering frame or a short cheese reveal to create immediate motion.
firstSecond.placement: Primary claim in the upper third; smaller dish name directly beneath it. Keep both clear of the food.
firstSecond.claimHandling: Present the rounded figures as label-based estimates for one bowl, not as physically verified results.

hierarchy.style: Large, bold, condensed or heavy sans serif in uppercase or strong title case.
Smaller, lighter sans serif with generous spacing.
Compact bold sans serif, one short label at a time.
Small but legible regular sans serif on a solid or translucent panel.
hierarchy.content: Label-based estimate per bowl. Check purchased labels.

typography.principles: Use no more than two type styles. Preserve a strong size difference between headline and supporting copy. Avoid reproducing the references' exact type combinations, chart design or branded marks.

overlayZones.upperThird: Primary nutrition hook and short recipe title. Best used when the bowl is positioned lower in frame.
overlayZones.sideZone: Short ingredient callouts beside a hand, pack or measured ingredient; keep the central cooking action unobstructed.
overlayZones.lowerThird: Captions, one-line method prompts and the final label-check caveat. Use a high-contrast backing when footage is busy.
overlayZones.fullFrameCard: Use for the four-ingredient list or nutrition methodology. Keep it visually simpler than the dense reference recipe pages.
avoid: Covering the melted-cheese focal point with text.
Placing small copy over textured food.
Stacking headline, captions, ingredient list and disclaimer in the same zone.
Using creator logos, page counters or replicated chart layouts from the references.

transitions.supportedApproach: Favor direct cuts between food actions and a clean cut to any information card. The frames emphasize clear state changes rather than elaborate effects.
options: Action match from pouring passata to stirring the bowl.
Cut on hand movement between ingredient additions.
Hard cut from preparation to a static nutrition card.
Return cut from the card to a close spoon lift or melted-cheese detail.
transitions.avoid: Do not infer or imitate creator-specific transition effects that are not visible in the still frames.

candidateNotes: All quantities are for one bowl: 235g drained cannellini beans, 100g lighter mozzarella, 150g passata and 50g spinach.
Calculated basis supplied: 40.025g protein and a fibre lower bound of 15.69g per serving.
Round the consumer-facing hook to 40g protein and 15g fibre, while retaining the label-based estimate caveat.
Because the recipe has not been physically tested, do not make claims about exact cook time, final texture, cheese pull or guaranteed appearance.
Show supermarket-style ingredients generically and avoid implying endorsement by a specific retailer or brand.
A useful evidence frame can show the four quantities and the line: 'Estimated from product labels; values vary by purchase.'
Keep the final serving visibly singular so the nutrition claim clearly refers to one bowl.
The concept should borrow only broad reference traits—food-dominant framing, strong top headline, separated information cards and restrained camera movement—not exact compositions or imagery.
